title: Demonstrate knowledge of and produce word processing documents using basic functions

lessons.title: Starting a document and saving it
lessons.html:
What a word processor does

A word processor is a computer program for typing letters, reports and forms. Common ones are Microsoft Word, LibreOffice Writer and Google Docs. On a seed farm you may use it to type a trial report, a notice for the workers' board, or a letter to a seed buyer.

Opening the program

  1. Switch on the computer and log in with your own user name and password.
  2. Click the Start button or the program icon.
  3. Choose Blank document to start a new page.

Parts of the screen

  • Title bar at the top shows the name of the file.
  • Menu or ribbon holds the buttons, such as File, Home and Insert.
  • Cursor is the blinking line. Your typing appears where the cursor is.
  • Scroll bar on the side moves you up and down the page.

Typing

Type normally. The program moves to the next line by itself. Press Enter only when you want a new paragraph. Use Backspace to remove the letter to the left of the cursor and Delete to remove the letter to the right.

Saving your work

Save early and save often. If the power goes off during load shedding, work that is not saved is lost.

  1. Click File, then Save As.
  2. Choose the right folder, for example Trials > 2026 > Maize.
  3. Give the file a clear name, such as Maize trial block 3 report March 2026.
  4. Click Save.

After the first save, press Ctrl + S every few minutes to save again. A clear file name helps your supervisor find the file later. Do not use names like Doc1 or New.

Closing

When you are done, save, then click File > Close. If the program asks "Do you want to save changes?", read the question carefully before you click.

lessons.title: Editing and formatting text
lessons.html:
Making changes to text

Editing means changing words. Formatting means changing how the words look. Both make a document easy to read.

Selecting text

Before you change text, you must select it. Click at the start of the words, hold the left mouse button and drag to the end. The selected text turns a different colour. Double-click selects one word. Ctrl + A selects the whole document.

Copy, cut and paste

  • Copy (Ctrl + C) keeps the text where it is and makes a copy.
  • Cut (Ctrl + X) removes the text so you can move it.
  • Paste (Ctrl + V) puts the copied or cut text where the cursor is.
  • Undo (Ctrl + Z) takes back your last action if you make a mistake.

Formatting buttons

ButtonWhat it does
BMakes text bold, good for headings
IMakes text slanted (italic)
UUnderlines text
Font sizeMakes letters bigger or smaller
AlignMoves text to the left, centre or right

Use one or two fonts only. A heading can be size 14 and bold. Normal text can be size 11 or 12. A notice for the workers' board can use bigger letters so people can read it from a distance.

Lists and tables

Use the bullet or number button to make a list, for example the steps to clean a seed planter. Use Insert > Table to make rows and columns, for example to show trial plot numbers and germination results.

Spell check

Words with a wavy red line may be spelt wrong. Right-click the word to see suggestions. The computer does not know every farm word or cultivar name, so check names and numbers yourself. A wrong number in a seed trial report can cause a big problem.

lessons.title: Printing and looking after files
lessons.html:
Getting the document ready to print

Before you print, check the page layout. Click Layout or Page Setup.

  • Paper size: in South Africa we normally use A4.
  • Orientation: Portrait is tall. Landscape is wide, which is useful for big tables.
  • Margins: the white space around the edges. Normal margins are fine for most work.

Headers, footers and page numbers

A header or footer is text that shows on every page. Put the farm name, the date and page numbers there. Click Insert > Page Number. Page numbers help when a long report is printed and the pages get mixed up.

Print preview and printing

  1. Click File > Print.
  2. Look at the preview on the right. Check that tables fit on the page and nothing is cut off.
  3. Choose the correct printer.
  4. Choose how many copies and which pages you want.
  5. Click Print.

Paper and ink cost money. Print only what you need, and check the preview first so you do not print the same thing twice.

Looking after your files

  • Keep files in folders with clear names, for example by year and crop.
  • Use Save As with a new name when you want a new version, so the old one stays safe.
  • Make a backup copy on a memory stick, a server or cloud storage, as your supervisor tells you.
  • Never open files from unknown memory sticks or emails. They can carry viruses.
  • Do not share your password with anyone.

Working safely at the computer

Sit up straight with your feet flat. Keep the screen at eye level. Rest your eyes every 20 to 30 minutes by looking at something far away. Keep drinks away from the keyboard.

Key points

  • Save with a clear file name in the right folder, and save often.
  • Select text first, then edit or format it.
  • Check spelling, names and numbers yourself.
  • Use print preview before printing.
  • Keep backups and protect your password.
